content.value_statement: Backlink sources can be difficult to assess and compare. This skill uses backlink-guard to gather evidence and summarize link opportunities and risks.
actual_capabilities: Find potential link opportunities from keyword search results.
Vet candidate sites and explain their reported risk and reach.
Verify whether a published page links to a target site.
Summarize backlink profiles, referring domains, and reported spam signals.
Compare competitor referring domains and early link sources.
Report AI Overview citations and sampled assistant answers.
limitations: The command line package must be installed or run separately.
Some signals require provider API keys and paid requests.
Site checks can fail or omit information; the tool cannot detect every private link sale.
Results are estimates and do not represent an official Google verdict.

use_cases.title: Vet a directory
use_cases.description: Compare candidate directories before spending time or money on a listing.

use_cases.title: Audit a backlink profile
use_cases.description: Review referring domains, repeated anchors, and reported spam signals.

use_cases.title: Compare competitors
use_cases.description: Find sites linking to competitors but not to your project.

prompt_templates.title: Check a site
prompt_templates.prompt: Vet [site] as a potential listing source and explain missing signals.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a listing
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether [listing URL] links to [target domain] and describe the link placement.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the backlinks for [domain], show evidence for each flag, and estimate any paid costs before running.

prompt_templates.title: Compare competitors
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [domain] with [competitor domains], identify shared link opportunities, and explain exclusions and costs before running.

output_examples.input: Vet a directory for my project.
output_examples.output: Example result: Look first. The page check was blocked, so its link quality remains unknown.
Example result: A link was found in the page body and marked nofollow. Confirm the page and attributes before acting.

best_practices: Review the exact package release before running it.
Approve estimated costs before any paid request.
Check the evidence and missing signals before making a decision.
anti_patterns: Treating a score as an official search engine verdict.
Submitting links in bulk or buying followed links.
Sharing API keys in prompts or reports.

faq.question: Does this skill submit listings?
faq.answer: The documented tool does not submit listings. Follow each site's contribution rules.

faq.question: Are API keys required?
faq.answer: Keys are optional for page checks. Paid provider signals require the relevant key.

faq.question: Are paid requests automatic?
faq.answer: The instructions require an estimated cost and user approval before each paid run.

faq.question: Can the tool verify a live link?
faq.answer: Yes. It reports whether a link was found and describes its attributes and placement.

faq.question: Does it detect every risky site?
faq.answer: No. Failed checks and private link sales can leave important information unavailable.

faq.question: Where does it store state?
faq.answer: The documented default is a hidden directory in the user's home folder. An environment variable can change the location.
